docs.title: Send_Clear_Error
docs.text:
ID 1host → driver0 bytesPython: Send_Clear_Error()

Clears the error flags and goes to idle. An error whose cause is still present comes straight back. A calibration error is cleared only by calibrating. A gripper E-stop comes back until the E-stop bit of Send_gripper_data_pack is 0 again.

The driver does not answer this command.

docs.title: Send_Watchdog
docs.text:
ID 15host → driver5 bytesPython: Send_Watchdog()

Sets the watchdog: when the time runs out the driver reports a watchdog error and stops. Every valid motion frame (Send_data_pack_1, Send_data_pack_PD, Send_data_pack_HALL, Send_gripper_data_pack) and every status request the driver answers resets it; the setting frames (gains, limits, Idle, Clear, Save, Settings and Send_Watchdog itself) do not. 0 turns it off (the default). The action byte is stored but not acted on by this firmware: the driver always stops into its idle behaviour. Send_Save_config keeps the watchdog, and a kept watchdog runs from power-up: a host that sends no motion frame or status request within the time finds the driver in watchdog error, and clears it with Send_Clear_Error.

5 bytes

Byte Bit Field Type Meaning 0-3 Time unsigned 32-bit ms; 0 = off 4 Action unsigned 8-bit 0 idle, 1 hold, 2 brake (stored only)

The driver does not answer this command.

docs.title: UART commands
docs.text: Every command the firmware release this site describes understands over the serial port. The kind, the argument type, the mode a command enters and what it prints are read from the firmware; the descriptions are written by hand. Over UART explains the protocol.

docs.title: Syntax
docs.text:
#<Name> [number]
  • A Set/Get command sets the value when a number follows and prints the current value either way.
  • A Get command only prints.
  • An Action command does something; a number after it is ignored. The exceptions are #Idle and #PWM: with a number they are answered Unknown command.
  • Names are case-sensitive, at most 19 characters; the number at most 19; the line ends with LF (CR before it is fine). 256000 baud, 8N1, 3.3 V.
  • A name the parser does not know is answered Unknown command.

From firmware 105 the reset lands in the bootloader, which waits 2 s for a flashing host and then starts the firmware again. nothing #Tlim Set/Get int: temperature in °C The temperature at which the temperature error is raised; 75 by default. Temp limit N #Default Action Writes the factory defaults to the EEPROM and loads them: the serial number, hardware version and batch date; the CAN ID (0); the gripper flag, heartbeat, watchdog and thermistor (off); the motor parameters and the calibration (cleared); every gain and limit. See Defaults. Loaded default config! #Temp Get Prints the thermistor temperature. °C, or Temp Off while the thermistor is disabled #Term Set/Get int: 0 or 1 Enables the thermistor measurement and the temperature error (off by default). the setting #Mode Get Prints the control mode. The voltage-torque mode prints Gripper mode; HALL, the angle-offset search, open-loop steps (gosteps) and gripper mode print nothing. Idle mode, Position control, Speed control, Current control, PD control, Open loop, Gripper mode, Gripper calib mode #Vbus Get Prints the supply voltage. mV #Error Get Prints which errors are active. No errors! or In error state! followed by one line per active error #Clear Action Clears the errors and goes to idle. An error whose cause is still present comes straight back; a calibration error is cleared only by calibrating (or #Calibrated 1). Enters idle mode. Clear errors #Iabc Get Prints the phase currents. Ia, Ib in mA #PWM Get Prints the PWM duty values. the duties #Help Action Prints a short command reference. Added in firmware 106. the reference #Info Get Prints the hardware version, batch date and firmware version, the control loop's execution time, the CAN ID, the calibration state, the thermistor and the supply voltage, the phase direction, phase order and commutation direction, and the motor parameters (pole pairs, angle offset, R, L, Kt, KV). Not the serial number (SERNUM), the gains (Param) or the errors (Error). the report #Param Get Prints every gain of every loop. the gains #Cyc Set/Get int: interval in ms (0 = off) Sends position, speed and Iq on its own every interval: $ <position> <speed> <Iq>; for BetterSerialPlotter. Cyclic disabled when turned off #Cyca Set/Get int: interval in ms (0 = off) Like Cyc, in the Arduino plotter format Position:x,Speed:y,Iq:z. Cyclic disabled when turned off #CANID Set/Get int: 0 to 13 The CAN node ID. Use 0 to 13: the firmware accepts 14 and 15, but the bootloader reserves them and a driver on one of those cannot be updated over CAN. Kept over a power cycle after Save, which also writes it into the bootloader's board ID. the ID, or Invalid CAN ID #SERNUM Set/Get int: number The serial number. This firmware does not read it back from the EEPROM at power-up: it reports 1 until set, and Save writes the value in RAM over the stored one. Serial number is: N #Activate Action Sets the activated flag. Controller activated #Pullconfig Get Prints the whole configuration on one line, for Motor GUI. the configuration #LED Set/Get int: 0 or 1 Turns the status LED on or off. the LED state

docs.title: Getting help
docs.text:
• Questions and discussion: the Source Robotics Discord.
  • A problem with the driver or the firmware: an issue in the firmware repository; see Report a problem for what to include.
  • A mistake on a page of this site: every page ends with a link to edit it and one to report it; see Contributing.
  • Orders and hardware: source-robotics.com.

Before you ask, Troubleshooting goes through the common symptoms, and #Info tells most of what anyone will ask you for.

docs.title: Contributing
docs.text: This documentation lives in Source-Robotics/STEPFOC-docs. A small fix can be made from the browser: the Edit it on GitHub link at the end of every page opens the page's source, and GitHub turns your change into a pull request. For anything larger, open an issue first.

docs.title: How the site is built
docs.text:
• The pages are Markdown, built with MkDocs and the Material theme; the repository's README.md says how to preview it locally.
  • The site describes one firmware release, named in versions.yml. The command IDs, frame lengths, the UART command list and the defaults in the Reference are read from the firmware's source at that release's tag by tools/sync_firmware.py; do not edit those facts in the pages. The descriptions of the commands are in docs/includes/can_commands.yml and uart_commands.yml.
  • Every push runs a strict build (a broken link fails it) and the tool tests. A push to main publishes the site under its firmware version with mike.

docs.title: House rules
docs.text:
• Facts come from the firmware. When a page and the firmware disagree, the firmware is right; fix the page, or report the firmware.
  • Spell commands exactly as the firmware does, even where the spelling looks wrong.
  • Write for someone who has the driver in front of them and wants to do one thing: say what to do, in order, then why.
  • Three kinds of boxes: a note, a notice (damage) and a danger (injury). Use them for those, not for emphasis.
  • Images: under 2400 px on the long side, with a caption that says what the reader should see.

docs.title: Report a problem
docs.text:
Open an issue in the firmware repository for the driver and its firmware, or in Spectral-BLDC-Python for the Python library. Include:

  1. The output of #Info, #Param and #Error, copied from the terminal. They carry the hardware and firmware version, the motor parameters, the calibration state, the gains and limits, and the errors.
  2. The motor: type, and the #R, #L, #PP you entered.
  3. The supply: voltage, and whether it has a current limit.
  4. What you did and what happened: the commands, in order, and the driver's answers; the calibration log if it is about calibration.
  5. How it is wired: a photo of the board on the motor and of the cables helps more than a description.

For a problem with this documentation, the Report it link at the end of the page opens an issue in the documentation repository with the page already named.
